en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for possessing the most perfect cone shape of any volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered species endemic only to the tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique body of water because it contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller crater lake.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting hundreds of diverse marine species.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry summer season.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over two thousand years ago for agriculture.
The tamaraw is a small, endangered mammal endemic to Mindoro, distinguished by its unique V-shaped horns and dark brown fur.
The Tabon Caves in Palawan yielded the Tabon Man skull cap, representing one of the oldest known human remains in the Philippines.
Mount Pinatubo in Zambales famously erupted in 1991, producing one of the largest volcanic explosions of the twentieth century.
